notes.text: Saul’s victory over the Ammonites confirms his kingship.
Jabesh-gilead was probably east of the Jordan River near the western edge of the Gilead mountains.
To make a treaty is literally “to cut a treaty,” which usually involved sacrificial animals. But Nahash demands to “cut” the treaty with the men’s eyes.
There were probably strong blood ties between Jabesh-gilead and Gibeah (see Judg. 21:12). The 42-mile (68-km) journey from Jabesh to Gibeah may have taken two days.
As in 10:6 (see note there), the Spirit of God rushed upon Saul, and he is filled with power like one of the judges (Judg. 3:10; 6:34; 11:29; 14:6).
Bezek was probably on the opposite side of the Jordan from Jabesh.
Give ourselves up to you can also mean “march out to you.” The speech of the men is deliberately unclear.
This ceremony at the worship center of Gilgal seems to be a religious coronation, as opposed to the political recognition in 10:17–25.
